subject: Draft: MAP boilerplate + technical acceptance checkpoints
body_text:
--- Message 1 (2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00) ---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@helium.ai>, Tom Herrera <tomh@novalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Draft: MAP boilerplate + technical acceptance checkpoints

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our agreement, I pulled together a first-pass MAP boilerplate focused on a 30/60 close window and a concise set of technical acceptance checkpoints that align to NovaLabs’ pilot goals. The intent: make the MAP small enough to drive momentum (week-by-week owners) while still capturing the gating criteria your infra team needs to validate.

What I’ve attached / linked:
- MAP-template-v1.gdoc — lightweight MAP with week-by-week milestones, success metrics, and stakeholder roster.
- technical-acceptance-checklist.xlsx — focused checks (networking, KV cache behavior, request/response sampling, observability hooks).
- week0-stakeholder-roles.csv — simple RACI for the first 14 days.

Requesting two things from your side:
1) Alicia: confirm whether the acceptance checklist covers the right infra owners and if any additional compliance checks are required (e.g., region-specific data residency for the pilot).
2) Tom: can we lock a 60-minute technical sync with your infra lead next Wed (Oct 6)? I’ve proposed an agenda in the GDoc — primarily to validate the acceptance tests and timeline.

Proposed next steps from our side (Jonas / Marissa / Karthik):
- Iterate MAP-template-v1 with your comments by EOD Mon (Oct 4).
- Run a short readiness-run through the acceptance checklist with our infra engineer to ensure it is reproducible.

If that works, I’ll update the GDoc and convert the acceptance checklist into a lightweight runbook so your team can execute tests during week 0.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP-template-v1.gdoc (link)]
[Attachment: technical-acceptance-checklist.xlsx]
---

--- Message 2 (2026-09-30T10:25:00-07:00) ---
From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@helium.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Herrera <tomh@novalabs.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 10:25 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Draft: MAP boilerplate + technical acceptance checkpoints

Jonas —

Thanks for sharing this so quickly. I skimmed the MAP and the checklist — overall looks good and very pragmatic. A few quick notes from my side:
- Data residency: NovaLabs requires EU region storage for the pilot dataset (we’ll provide a subset). Please mark that as a must for the acceptance criteria.
- Observability: Can you add an example of the trace we should expect (token-level latency profile) so our SREs can correlate Redwood traces to our existing traces?
- SLA expectations: we’re comfortable with a canary/safety SLA during pilot, but we’ll need committed latencies for the dedicated phase — happy to hash details in the sync.

We can do Wed Oct 6 10:00–11:00 PT for the tech sync. I’ve invited Tom’s infra lead but he may need a calendar nudge.

Alicia
Head of Integrations
Helium AI

Jonas / team —

This is a great starter. A couple of internal coordination notes on owners and timing:
- I’ll own week 0 runbook creation and the run-through with our infra engineer (Chad). Chad will reproduce the checklist locally and capture exact command snippets for each step.
- Karthik — can you add the runtime config options we typically include for low-latency pilot runs (batch window defaults, KV cache warmup steps, and a quick note on quantization flags)? I think that will help NovaLabs reproduce results without diving into runtime internals.
- I’ll also add a short stakeholder readout slide for the Oct 13 exec checkpoint (1 slide, 3 bullets).

I attached a CSV with a proposed week0 stakeholder list (owners + backups). We should confirm roles before AJ’s infra interview next week.

Thanks —
Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 (2026-09-30T13:05:00-07:00) ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Barnes <alicia@helium.ai>, Tom Herrera <tomh@novalabs.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 1:05 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Draft: MAP boilerplate + technical acceptance checkpoints

Marissa / Jonas —

Adding the runtime config suggestions now. High-level notes I pasted into the GDoc:
- Batch sizing: start conservative (max batch size 8, 50ms batch window) for the pilot to keep tail latency tight.
- KV cache warmup: recommend a short synthetic load (1 minute, interleaved requests) before acceptance tests to primeline hit rates.
- Quantization: use 8-bit asymmetric where possible for dedicated cost testing; note that some of NovaLabs’ ops may prefer float16 for inference stability.

I also created a short test snippet to validate prefix caching behavior and added it to the checklist as a reproducible step (command + expected log lines).

I’ll sync with Chad off-thread to ensure the snippets run in our infra harness.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: runtime-flags-snippet.txt]

--- Message 5 (2026-09-30T15:42:00-07:00) ---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 3:42 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Draft: MAP boilerplate + technical acceptance checkpoints

Alicia / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turns and the calendar confirmation. Updated items in the GDoc:
- Data residency checkbox (EU) marked as MUST.
- Added an example trace snippet and a short note on correlating token latency with your tracing IDs.
- Karthik’s runtime flags and the KV cache snippet are in the checklist as reproducible steps.

Agenda for Wed Oct 6 10:00 PT (tech sync):
1) Quick intros (5m)
2) Walk acceptance checklist and demo a live KV cache warmup (20m)
3) Observability correlation: show example trace and where to find per-token metrics (15m)
4) Risk & SLA conversation for dedicated phase (15m)
5) Confirm owners / next actions (5m)

Action items:
- Alicia: confirm EU data subset delivery ETA (week of Oct 4).
- Tom: confirm who from NovaLabs SRE will join the sync (name + calendar invite).
- Marissa: share the week0 runbook doc by EOD Mon Oct 4.

I’ll publish the MAP-template-v1 to the shared folder and convert the checklist into a short runbook format for execution during week 0.

Best —
Jonas
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
